$comment: The published-documentation ratchet (#75 WP01, #129).
Every public attribute and public method of a tagged declaration must carry a description:
the React generator copies attributes[].description into the emitted prop docs and the
class-level `## Methods` block, so one with none ships `/** undefined */` into a consumer's
editor. check-manifest-content.mjs asserts the descriptions are non-empty.
THIS FILE IS THE ANTI-VACUITY HALF, and it exists because the first version of that gate
did not have one. It counted DECLARATIONS, not items, so a manifest with five tagged
elements and zero attributes and zero methods printed
✅ 0 public attribute(s) and method(s) across 5 element(s) all carry a description.
— a green line over an empty set, in the gate whose own docstring names that defect class.
Both pre-merge lenses found it independently. Same shape as expected-parts.json, and the
same reason.
EXACT EQUALITY, not shrink-only. Removing a documented property or method is an API change
and should be a deliberate line in the same commit; adding one likewise. Either direction
silently moving is what this refuses. If a count changes, change it here and say why in the
commit message.
Counts are of the PUBLISHED surface as the wrapper generator sees it: attributes[] entries,
and members[] of kind `method` that are not private/protected and do not start with `#`.
Note that `state: true` properties are deliberately absent from attributes[] — they observe
no attribute and cannot be delivered on a first render under ssrSafe — so they are not
counted here either. See scripts/normalise-manifest.mjs.

#77 adds <sk-site-footer> with FIVE attributes and zero methods: wordmark, tagline, legal, column-one-heading and column-two-heading. Every one is a string, which is the operator's ruling on #77 working around a constraint this ratchet's sibling gate enforces — the React wrappers' ssrSafe mode delivers first-render props as ATTRIBUTES, which carry only strings, so structured data would not survive. The link ITEMS are slotted instead. An earlier revision of this entry recorded 0/0 for a slot-only design that contradicted that ruling; the rebuild is why the numbers moved.
